svg.title: Law and policy responses, 1957–2026

g.aria-label: PAROS (UNGA agenda item), 1981 to present. First PAROS resolutions adopted Dec 9, 1981 (UNGA 36/97 C; 36/99). CD Ad Hoc Committee on PAROS met 1985-94. No treaty has resulted.
CD Ad Hoc Committee on PAROS, 1985 to 1994. Conference on Disarmament committee re-established annually 1985-1994; mandate lapsed.
OEWG on space threats, 2022 to 2023. Open-ended working group under Res. 76/231; ended without a consensus report.

Limited Test Ban Treaty, Aug 5, 1963. Signed Aug 5, 1963; in force Oct 10, 1963. Bans nuclear tests in outer space. It followed Starfish Prime; fallout concerns and the Cuban Missile Crisis were also drivers. Has 3D scene.
Outer Space Treaty, Jan 27, 1967. Opened Jan 27, 1967; in force Oct 10, 1967. Art. IV bars nuclear weapons and WMD in orbit; silent on conventional ASATs.
ABM Treaty Art. XII, May 26, 1972. Bars interference with the other party's 'national technical means' of verification (bilateral; US withdrew 2002).

ITU Constitution Arts. 45 & 48, Dec 22, 1992. Adopted Geneva 1992; in force July 1, 1994. Art. 45 prohibits harmful interference; Art. 48 gives military radio installations 'complete freedom' (the core gap for jamming). The Radio Regulations sit beneath the Constitution. Has 3D scene.
PPWT draft (Russia-China), Feb 12, 2008. Draft treaty on preventing placement of weapons in outer space, tabled at the CD. Does not cover ground-based (direct-ascent) ASATs.
PPWT updated draft, Jun 10, 2014. Revised draft; still silent on ground-based ASATs and testing.
Tallinn Manual 2.0 (soft law), Feb 1, 2017. Soft law. Expert manual on international law applicable to cyber operations. Not binding law.
UNGA 75/36, Dec 7, 2020. Reducing space threats through norms, rules and principles of responsible behaviour.
McGill (MILAMOS) Manual Vol. I (soft law), Jan 1, 2022. Soft law. Expert manual on international law applicable to military uses of outer space. Not binding law.

US DA-ASAT test moratorium, Apr 18, 2022. US commits not to conduct destructive direct-ascent ASAT missile tests. Followed by Canada, New Zealand, Japan, Germany, UK, France and others; SWF counts 38 states in total. Has 3D scene.
UNGA 77/41 (DA-ASAT tests), Dec 7, 2022. Calls on states to commit not to conduct destructive direct-ascent ASAT missile tests. Adopted 155-9-9.
Woomera Manual (soft law), Jan 1, 2024. Soft law. Expert manual on international law of military space operations. Not binding law.

Russian veto: nuclear weapons in orbit, Apr 24, 2024. Russia vetoed a US-Japan draft reaffirming OST Art. IV (no nuclear weapons in orbit). Vote 13-1-1 (China abstained). The draft did not concern DA-ASAT testing.

ITU RRB: 'grave concern' (Sweden, France), Jul 1, 2024. Radio Regulations Board expressed grave concern about intentional harmful interference to Swedish and French satellites that seemed to originate from earth stations in Russia. Has 3D scene.

ICAO: Russia's GNSS interference breaches Chicago Convention, Oct 1, 2025. ICAO found GNSS interference originating in Russia infringed the 1944 Chicago Convention, condemned it, and called on Russia to meet its obligations. Has 3D scene.

ITU RRB 100th meeting: urges Russia to cease RNSS interference, Nov 1, 2025. Board again urged Russia to immediately cease harmful interference to radionavigation-satellite service receivers in Estonia, Finland, Latvia and Lithuania. Has 3D scene.

svg.text: * soft law (expert manual) · bars = negotiation spans
Legal band. Data: ledger built from SWF Global Counterspace Capabilities (9th ed., Apr. 2026) and cited sources. Companion to Space Security Law.
